title: Alpha Star and Exceptional Character Restriction
body_html:
Alpha Star and Exceptional Character Restriction

The homomorphism \[ \alpha:S'_{\lambda'}\to S_\lambda \] from the residual fiber stabilizer calculation epipelagic_theta.residual_fiber_stabilizer induces a character map \[ \alpha^*:\operatorname{Char}(S_\lambda)\to \operatorname{Char}(S'_{\lambda'}),\qquad \alpha^*(\chi)=\chi\circ\alpha. \] Although \(\alpha\) depends on the chosen \(\bar w\in X_{\lambda,\lambda'}\), the induced map on Grothendieck groups is independent of \(\bar w\), because different choices are conjugate in the residual fiber calculation.

In the exceptional unitary equal-rank case, not every character of \(S_\lambda\) occurs. A character \(\chi\) contributes to \(C[X_{\lambda,\lambda'}]\) exactly when its restriction to the stabilizer subgroup \(S_{\bar w}\subset S_\lambda\) is trivial.
proof_html: The independence follows from the orbit statement in epipelagic_theta.residual_fiber_stabilizer: replacing \(\bar w\) conjugates the graph subgroup defining \(\alpha\). The exceptional restriction follows from the identification \(X_{\lambda,\lambda'}\simeq S_\lambda/S_{\bar w}\); the regular representation of this quotient contains precisely the characters trivial on \(S_{\bar w}\).
